title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Letter of Credit Dispute Cases

articles.content_en: Article 1 The letter of credit dispute cases referred to in these Provisions shall refer to disputes arising in the process of issuance, notification, amendment, revocation, confirmation, negotiation, reimbursement, or other links of a letter of credit.

Article 2 When a People's Court tries a letter of credit dispute case, if the parties have agreed to apply relevant international practice or other provisions, such agreement shall be followed; if the parties have no agreement, the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits of the International Chamber of Commerce or other relevant international practice shall apply.

Article 3 These Provisions shall apply to disputes over debts arising between the applicant and the issuing bank from the application for issuance of a letter of credit, disputes between the principal and the agent arising from the entrustment to issue a letter of credit, disputes arising from the provision of security by a guarantor for an application for issuance or entrustment for issuance of a letter of credit, and disputes arising from financing under a letter of credit.

Article 4 Disputes over debts arising from an application for issuance of a letter of credit, disputes over entrustment to issue a letter of credit, guarantee disputes arising therefrom, and disputes arising from financing under a letter of credit shall be governed by the relevant laws of the People's Republic of China, unless the parties to a foreign-related contract have otherwise agreed on the applicable law.

Article 5 After the issuing bank has made a commitment to pay, accept, or perform other obligations under the letter of credit, the issuing bank shall perform the obligation to pay within the time limit prescribed by the letter of credit, provided that the documents appear on their face to be in conformity with the terms and conditions of the letter of credit and with each other. Where a party raises a defense based on the underlying transaction between the applicant and the beneficiary, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the circumstances under Article 8 of these Provisions exist.

Article 6 When a People's Court, in trying a letter of credit dispute case, involves examination of documents, it shall do so in accordance with the relevant international practice or other provisions agreed upon by the parties to apply; if the parties have no agreement, it shall determine whether the documents appear on their face to be in conformity with the terms and conditions of the letter of credit and with each other in accordance with the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits of the International Chamber of Commerce and the relevant standards established by the International Chamber of Commerce.
Where the documents under a letter of credit are not entirely consistent on their face with the terms and conditions of the letter of credit or with each other, but such inconsistency does not give rise to ambiguity between them, it shall not be deemed a discrepancy.

Article 7 The issuing bank shall have the independent right and obligation to examine the documents, and shall have the right to make its own determination as to whether the documents appear on their face to conform to the terms and conditions of the letter of credit and with each other, and to decide on its own whether to accept or reject discrepancies between the documents and the terms and conditions of the letter of credit or between the documents.
After discovering discrepancies under the letter of credit, the issuing bank may decide on its own whether to contact the applicant to accept the discrepancies. The applicant's decision whether to accept the discrepancies shall not affect the issuing bank's final decision whether to accept the discrepancies, unless the issuing bank and the applicant have otherwise agreed.
Where the issuing bank expressly indicates to the beneficiary that it accepts the discrepancies, it shall bear liability for payment.
Where the issuing bank rejects the discrepancies, and the beneficiary requests the issuing bank to bear liability for payment under the letter of credit on the ground that the applicant has accepted the discrepancies, the People's Court shall not support it.

Article 9 Where the applicant, the issuing bank, or any other interested party discovers circumstances as described in Article 8 of these Provisions and considers that such circumstances would cause irreparable harm to it, it may apply to the People's Court with jurisdiction for suspension of payment of the amount under the letter of credit.

Article 12 After a People's Court accepts an application for suspension of payment of the amount under a letter of credit, it must render a ruling within forty-eight hours; if it rules to suspend payment, it shall immediately begin enforcement.
A People's Court's ruling to suspend payment of the amount under a letter of credit shall list the applicant, the respondent, and the third party.

Article 13 Where a party objects to a People's Court's ruling on suspension of payment of the amount under a letter of credit, it may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration within ten days from the date of service of the written ruling. The People's Court at the next higher level shall render a ruling within ten days from the date of receipt of the application for reconsideration.
During the period of reconsideration, enforcement of the original ruling shall not be suspended.

Article 14 In the process of trying a letter of credit fraud case, a People's Court may, when necessary, try the letter of credit dispute together with the underlying transaction dispute.
Where a party prosecutes on the ground of underlying transaction fraud, it may list the issuing bank, negotiating bank, or other interested party in the letter of credit legal relationship related to the case as a third party; the third party may apply to participate in the proceedings, and the People's Court may also notify the third party to participate in the proceedings.

Article 15 Where a People's Court, through substantive trial, finds that letter of credit fraud is constituted and that none of the circumstances under Article 10 of these Provisions exists, it shall adjudge to terminate payment of the amount under the letter of credit.

Article 16 Where a guarantor requests exemption from its guarantee liability on the ground that the issuing bank or the applicant accepted discrepancies without obtaining its consent, the People's Court shall not support it, unless the guarantee contract provides otherwise.

Article 17 Where the applicant and the issuing bank amend the letter of credit without obtaining the guarantor's consent, the guarantor shall bear guarantee liability only within the period and scope agreed upon in the original guarantee contract or prescribed by law, unless the guarantee contract provides otherwise.
Article 18 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2006.
